temporal_notes: Larvae collected from natural habitats in highland areas around Kisumu district; specific sampling dates are not reported. Manuscript received 3 December 2014 and published in 2015.
source_text: A. gambiae larvae were collected from natural habitats (>10 meters distance between any two habitats) in highland areas around the Kisumu district of Kenya where malaria is hyperendemic. More than half of mosquito larvae were successfully reared to adults in an insectary at the Kenya Medical Research Institute. The resulting 3–5-day post-emergence female mosquitoes were used for experiments. ... Genomic DNA was extracted from 7-day post-blood-fed mosquitoes using DNAzol ... The individual mosquito species was confirmed by the rDNA-PCR method [34].
